pages.title: Palindrome counting and its limits
pages.kicker: NOTE 07 · EXACT COUNT UNDER A SAMPLING MODEL

blocks.text: For independent uniform q-symbol strings of length n, ordinary palindromes have probability q^−floor(n/2). The example q = 4, n = 40 has probability exactly 2⁻⁴⁰.

blocks.label: Exact count under a sampling model
blocks.text: The probability is tied to the stated sampling model. Forty is the sequence length in the example, not a proved limit on the size of a sustainable biological alphabet.

Count free positions in a reversed string, then distinguish ordinary reversal from reverse complementation. An expected number of independent complete-string draws is not a guarantee for overlapping windows.
Before making a biophysical claim, specify a physical alphabet, pairing rule and measurable stability or decay criterion. The finite combinatorics supplies no biochemical feasibility result.

This note preserves the definitions and written derivation from the supplied mathematical fragments, reconstructed in the full collection. Its proof is given on the following page(s); no literature-priority claim is made.

pages.title: Forty positions, four symbols
pages.kicker: 01 · EXACT COUNTING AND THE BIOPHYSICS BOUNDARY

blocks.text: Assume each symbol is chosen independently and uniformly from an alphabet of integer size q ≥ 2. An ordinary palindrome reads identically under reversal. For a fixed length n ≥ 1, the first ceiling(n/2) symbols determine the rest.

The reciprocal is approximately 1.10 × 1012 independently sampled complete strings per first success in the geometric waiting model, including the successful draw. It is not a deterministic guarantee or an automatic formula for overlapping windows.

blocks.label: What the number 40 means
blocks.text: In the displayed example, 40 is the sequence length n and the alphabet size is q = 4. Taking q = 40 defines a different abstract counting experiment. Neither calculation establishes a maximum sustainable DNA alphabet, a chemical stability threshold or an optimal decay rate.

A DNA reverse-complement palindrome is a different condition. Under a fixed-point-free complement pairing and the same uniform independent model, an even length has probability q<super>−n/2</super>; an odd length is impossible because its central symbol would have to complement itself.

The suggested synthetic-alphabet and biophysics thread therefore remains a research direction. It needs an explicit physical model, measurable stability criteria and suitable evidence beyond this combinatorial count.
